To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) patch representations based on convolutional kernel networks can be learned without supervision and perform well on image retrieval, and (ii) they can be learned in a fraction of the time it takes to train a CNN for classification.

(1) patch descriptors learned without supervision can be used for image retrieval, (2) the best descriptor is obtained with a convolutional kernel network, and (3) the descriptor can be learned with a small amount of data and in a reasonable amount of time.
a) Patch-CKN performs well for patch and image matching, b) it is significantly more efficient to train and c) it outperforms SIFT and all other CNNs learned with artificially introduced supervision
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to learn a patch representation for image retrieval in an unsupervised fashion.

the following questions: How can we learn a patch representation that is able to capture the local stationary structures present in natural images? How can we use such a representation for instance-level image retrieval? And, how can we evaluate the performance of a patch descriptor for image retrieval?

the following questions: How to design convolutional neural networks for learning patch descriptors for image retrieval? Can we learn patch descriptors that are competitive with SIFT and faster to train?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our approach is able to learn better representations for image retrieval than SIFT, and that it is also able to learn better patch descriptors for retrieval than convolutional neural networks trained with supervision.
our proposed descriptor outperforms SIFT and other convolutional networks in terms of accuracy and speed of training.
Patch-CKN outperforms all other unsupervised descriptors in all experiments, including the state-of-the-art supervised CNNs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an unsupervised method for learning patch descriptors that is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance for image retrieval.
convolutional kernel networks can be successfully applied for unsupervised patch representation learning, leading to state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks.
convolutional neural networks are able to learn good descriptors for patch matching, even in the absence of supervision.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the success of CNNs for image classification does not necessarily carry over to unsupervised tasks and that new representations should be designed to take advantage of the inherent multi-scale properties of convolutional networks.
convolutional neural networks are able to model the local stationary structures in an unsupervised manner, and that this is enough to achieve excellent performance for patch retrieval.
, in the absence of supervision, CNNs trained with the patch retrieval task are able to learn good image descriptors, without any fine-tuning or retraining.
